The older guide omits the existing admin-expense 403 and illustrates can_select: true on assigned-sites. The route is administrator-only and assigned-sites does not calculate can_select. The main construction-site list computes a boolean.
Scramble can infer can_select as a string, salary worker_id as a string, and omit real 403 or business 500 conditions on some operations. Controllers, Resources and contract tests take precedence.

global_changes.title: DailyLog identity
global_changes.before: The API represented one responsible manager as owner.
global_changes.after: A single canonical log represents a site and date; participants are independent rows.
global_changes.client_impact: Share one DailyLog.id between managers at the same site/date.

global_changes.title: Daily participants
global_changes.before: One manager was represented on a DailyLog.
global_changes.after: An active assigned manager joins the canonical log; another manager can join it too.
global_changes.client_impact: Render the same shared children for both members.

global_changes.title: Multiple selections per day
global_changes.before: The client could look up a single log for a manager and date.
global_changes.after: The same manager can select and work with several sites on one day.
global_changes.client_impact: Store the ID returned for the selected site instead of using manager/date as a key.

global_changes.title: Legacy manager ID removed
global_changes.after: DailyLog JSON omits site_manager_id. Child attribution and legacy inputs remain where defined.
global_changes.client_impact: Remove this field only from DailyLog output models.

global_changes.title: Legacy manager relation removed
global_changes.after: DailyLog does not expose a singular manager relation.
global_changes.client_impact: Delete DailyLog owner parsing and avoid synthesizing it from the first participant.

global_changes.title: Plural manager representation
global_changes.before: No daily participants array was exposed.
global_changes.after: DailyLog.site_managers contains Worker fields plus nullable joined_at where loaded.
global_changes.client_impact: Parse the array for participation display; distinguish it from permanent site assignments.

global_changes.title: Child manager attribution
global_changes.before: Owner-style workflows commonly assumed the acting manager was also the record owner.
global_changes.after: Attribution stays with the child; created_by remains the original actor and later actors appear in audit.
global_changes.client_impact: Render attribution from each child record and preserve it on shared updates.

global_changes.title: Site selection
global_changes.before: Clients performed local selection or created/looked up a manager-specific log.
global_changes.after: POST /construction-sites/{constructionSite}/select creates or joins the canonical DailyLog.
global_changes.client_impact: Accept 200 or 201 and persist data.id as active.

global_changes.title: Shared daily data
global_changes.before: Child data and permissions followed legacy daily context and owner rules.
global_changes.after: Participants use the same attendance, expenses, notes, deliveries, subcontractors, attachments and machine records.
global_changes.client_impact: Use DailyLog ID and record ID for caches and writes; retain explicit attribution filters only where required.

global_changes.title: Pending assignment attribution
global_changes.before: Self-assignment could inherit the old DailyLog manager.
global_changes.after: A new self-assignment has null manager attribution until managerial action.
global_changes.client_impact: Accept nullable site_manager wire relation; never require a synthesized ID.

global_changes.title: Machine attendance confirmation
global_changes.before: Machine salary synchronization used managerial timestamps and legacy attribution.
global_changes.after: A self-assignment produces no salary row. Manager-authoritative start drives synchronization, and actual managerial attribution is used.
global_changes.client_impact: Represent pending operational reservations separately from salary attendance.

global_changes.title: Locked DailyLog
global_changes.before: Machine mutations and some other paths did not consistently enforce editability.
global_changes.after: Authorized reads remain available. Daily child mutations and machine create/update/delete/takeover/finish require an editable log.
global_changes.client_impact: Disable those actions while locked and respect backend rejection after stale reads.

global_changes.title: Daily membership access
global_changes.before: The singular manager or broad company access controlled some operations.
global_changes.after: SITE_MANAGER access follows company, daily membership, role and editability rules for the endpoint.
global_changes.client_impact: Handle 403 and treat filtered 200/404 results as legitimate.

global_changes.title: Company-scoped outputs
global_changes.before: Some lists, direct IDs and relation queries were broader than the caller’s company.
global_changes.after: Migrated routes scope data to the caller’s company.
global_changes.client_impact: Use active-company data and clear stale cross-company caches.

global_changes.title: Multiple attendance periods per day
global_changes.before: An ordinary worker was limited to one manual attendance per company and date.
global_changes.after: The daily attendance limit has been removed. Multiple non-overlapping periods on the same or different sites are valid for the same company and worker. An open attendance reserves time from its start until the local midnight following attendance.date. Salary uses exactly eight hours per open attendance.
global_changes.client_impact: Query GET /api/v1/workers/available with the proposed start, optional finish, and role. Use the returned WorkerResource list directly; remove all-workers-minus-any-attendance and day-level filters. Writes still recheck overlap.

global_changes.title: Machine release boundaries
global_changes.before: The previous implementation allowed manager-started open machine reservations past midnight.
global_changes.after: Machine manager periods use [start, finish); absent manager finish releases at local midnight at the end of the assignment date. Without manager start, the machine is reserved for its business date. Operator/driver finish does not release it.
global_changes.client_impact: Use machine availability endpoints and submit an explicit finish date for overnight shifts.

global_changes.title: Point-in-time worker availability
global_changes.before: The availability endpoint required started_at and queried an entire interval.
global_changes.after: No time parameters check the current instant. at checks a specified instant. started_at selects interval mode.
global_changes.client_impact: Call GET /api/v1/workers/available?role=worker for available now. Use at for an explicit point, or started_at and optional finished_at for a planned interval. Present server candidates directly; never subtract everyone with attendance that day.

global_changes.title: Default worker display order
global_changes.before: Worker display_order was introduced with default and minimum 1 and ascending numeric ordering. Both are now 0, and the normal group sorts last.
global_changes.after: Worker.display_order is a non-null integer, default 0. On create and update it is optional; send a JSON integer from 0 to 2147483647. Omitting it on update keeps the current value. Sending 0 removes manual priority. Duplicate values are allowed. The backend lists all positive manual priorities first, in ascending order, and then the normal group (0). Within each equal value it sorts by first_name, last_name, and id ascending. Preserve the backend order unless the user requests another supported sort. Explicit sort/direction on GET /workers takes precedence.
global_changes.client_impact: Parse Worker.display_order and preserve the server order in worker pickers. Send display_order only when the administrator sets it.
